subject: Recap: Migration pathway discovery — next steps and eval scope
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsive.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Migration pathway discovery — next steps and eval scope

Samir — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Below is a short recap of the pain, the goals we captured, and the suggested next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Heavy monthly spend on OpenAI/Anthropic for generation + embeddings; cost is brittle as usage grows.
- Rate limits and burst throttling cause user-facing latency issues during peak hours.
- Need deterministic behaviour for clinical-template generation (medical summaries) — hallucination risk is a blocker.
- PHI concerns: want tighter control over data residency and KMS.

Current stack we heard
- OpenAI for text-gen & chat (primary for consumer-facing flows).
- Anthropic for a subset of safety-sensitive reranking pipelines.
- Self-hosted Redis + Postgres for prompt state; embeddings stored in Pinecone today.
- CI/CD triggers deploy prompts + evaluation harness via a shared Google Drive.

Success criteria for a migration pilot
- P95 latency for single-shot generation <= 300ms for <1k tokens (edge latency targets).
- Token-unit cost reduction target: 2x-3x from current baseline (TBD after we get usage mix).
- No functional regressions on your critical prompt set (templates for discharge summaries).
- Privacy controls: keys + logs under your KMS and audit log access.

Compatibility requirements we noted
- Streaming + chunked outputs (for progress updates in the UI).
- Function/tool-calling semantics (structured outputs for downstream systems).
- Embedding fingerprint parity (we'll define eval to compare embedding quality).
- Low-effort SDK drop-in (python/ts) and clear migration guides for the ingestion paths to your existing infra (Redis + Pinecone).

Initial model shortlist we recommended during the call
- Llama 3 (instruction tuned, 70B) — for high-quality long-form generation.
- Mistral 7B Instruct (quantized variant) — low-cost generation for high-throughput routes.
- RedPajama-INCITE / RedPajama-Chat (smaller sizes) — fallback and regeneration templates.
(We will produce benchmarked profiles and a quantization suggestion per workload.)

Proposed next steps
- You: share the canonical prompt set + 50 representative production examples (anonymized/PHI-stripped) — we can run quality/regression evals.
- Us: run a lightweight compatibility suite (latency, cost estimate, embedding parity) and deliver a 2-week pilot plan.
- Security: we’ll share SOC 2 summary + high-level architecture for Private deployment options.
- Timeline: aim to have an evaluation report and pilot proposal by Apr 16 if we receive the prompt set by Apr 6.

Attachments included with this note:
- medsive-prompt-set-v1.csv (stub — please upload anonymized examples)
- redwood-compatibility-checklist.xlsx (high-level fields we’ll verify)

If this looks right I’ll schedule the eval kickoff with Marissa (solutions engineer) and outline access steps for your infra team.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0129

---

(Attachment stub: medsive-prompt-set-v1.csv)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsive.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medsive Engineering <eng@medsive.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 18:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Migration pathway discovery — next steps and eval scope

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmed items below and a couple clarifications: 

Confirmations
- We agree with the success criteria and the latency/cost targets as a starting point.
- We will anonymize and share the 50 examples; security will review PHI-stripping requirements (targeting Apr 5).

Clarifications/asks
- Procurement will need a one-page SOW + estimated spend range for the 2-week pilot to brief finance. Can you include a hosted vs. dedicated cost delta?
- Security: please include a link to your SOC 2 report and a short checklist for KMS/HSM compatibility.
- Integrations: our engineering lead asked whether Redwood supports live streaming to our socket layer (yes/no) and what the max concurrent connections per model instance are.

We’re broadly interested in private deployment but want to see the eval results first. If the initial pilot looks good, procurement will push for a dedicated capacity PO in Q2.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Medsive
samir.patel@medsive.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Ben
